averageUsableCapacity.note: Average usable capacity of the prison system, excluding 20 police cells and rented capacity.

visuals.vanishingCrime: The chart shows registered crimes per 1,000 inhabitants in the Netherlands from 1948 to 2025, peaking in 2002 at 93 per 1,000 and dropping to 45 per 1,000 in 2025, a 51.6% decline. Property crime remains the largest category at 25 per 1,000 in 2025.
visuals.clearance: In 1954 the solved share of crimes peaked at 75.0% while in 2025 it fell to 22.0%, a drop of 70.7%. Registered crimes per 1,000 inhabitants dropped from 93 in 2002 to 45 in 2025, a fall of 51.6%.
visuals.dock: The chart shows registered suspects by offence category in 2022, with property offences having the largest share of 24.6% of the categories shown.
visuals.courtroom: In 2022, 44.1% of prosecutor decisions were summons, down from 55.5% in 2001.
visuals.funnel: This funnel shows what happened to 810,550 crimes in 2022, with 33 per 100 leading to suspect registration and only 4 per 100 ending in a prison term. The steepest drop is between suspect registration (33 per 100) and summons (10 per 100).
visuals.sanctions: In 2022, 32.5% of Dutch court sanctions were prison sentences and 25.0% were community service, while in 2001 only 15.3% were community service and 30.5% were fines.
visuals.catch: The chart shows the share of registered suspects by sex. Men make up 83.0% of suspects while women make up 16.6%.
visuals.jail: In 2025 there are 9,700 detainees, a 36.2% drop from 2005, and 19.5% of them face sentences of 3 years or longer.
visuals.europe: The chart ranks 35 European countries by prison population per 100,000 inhabitants in 2024, with the Netherlands highlighted at 66.59 and 32nd place. Its prisons are 94.7% full, holding 11,948 of 12,614 available places.
